nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What health risks are associated with mosquito bites that DEET helps to prevent?
nodes.answer: DEET helps to protect against mosquito-borne illnesses such as malaria, zika virus, Lyme disease, spotted fever, and the Nile virus.
nodes.paragraph: T1 conditions resulted in more significant lipid formation than other test runs, making biofuel for DEET-contaminated wastewater a feasible alternative. Keywords Chlorella vulgaris, DEET, Acute toxicity, Biochemical composition, Removal Introduction N,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) is the main ingredi - ent used in products such as lotions, sprays, and mate - rials (towelettes and roll-ons) as insect repellent. DEET is very effective in deterring the biting of arthropods (mosquitoes and ticks). A third of American adults use DEET to protect themselves from mosquito-borne ill - nesses such as malaria, zika virus, Lyme disease, spotted fever, and the Nile virus [1, 2]. The DEET concentration in the products typically ranges between 5 and 99%, and it is approved for skin applications, not for ingestion, and is not employed in food-related contexts [3]. DEET functions by impeding the olfactory perception of these hematophagous insects toward the human scent. Follow - ing its initial development by the United States Army in 1946, DEET was subsequently licensed for civilian use in 1957 [4].

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Good health and well-being|Infectious diseases prevention and control|Vector control strategies_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the primary use of N,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET)?
nodes.answer: DEET is primarily used in personal care products as a preventive measure against mosquito-borne diseases.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract JN,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) is one of the significant chemical formulations used extensively in personal care products as a preventive measure against mosquito-borne diseases. It has been detected in the aquatic matrix at various concentrations from ng/L to mg/L. Chlorella vulgaris is one of the potential algal species for the treat - ment of wastewater containing personal care products, and this study investigates the acute toxicity and removal potential of Chlorella vulgaris in the removal of DEET with its effects on pigments and biochemical composition. The 96-h EC50 was calculated to be 17.4 mg/L, and the biochemical composition assessment revealed that lipid concentrations in Chlorella vulgaris increased until the tolerance limit. This investigation revealed that when DEET concentration crossed the tolerance limit (17.4 mg/L) in the medium, the pigments and biochemical concentrations reduced drastically, indicating Chlorella vulgaris inhibitory response beyond the tolerance limit, causing irreversible damage to the algal cells. Furthermore, Chlorella vulgaris removal potential at three different test runs, T1 (5 mg/L), T2 (10 mg/L), and T3 (25 mg/L) were studied. The most remarkable elimination in T1 test runs was 72% due to biodegra- dation, followed by T2 (35%) and T3 (15%).
